note: The Credit Information System Act (Republic Act No. 9510), section 4(h): negative information stays in the Credit Information Corporation's database not more than three years from when it's rectified by payment or settlement. Read on 2026-11-03 in the Supreme Court E-Library's text of the Act, the judiciary's own channel; until then it was read in LawPhil's copy, which said the same and is no longer cited. The Official Gazette's PDF answered 403 and the Corporation's own site a script page. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update.

sources.title: Supreme Court E-Library (Philippines), Republic Act No. 9510 (2008-10-31), An Act Establishing the Credit Information System, and for Other Purposes
sources.said: The negative information on a borrower as contained in the credit history files of borrowers should stay in the database of the Corporation unless sooner corrected, for not more than three (3) years from and after the date when the negative credit information was rectified through payment or liquidation of the debt, or through settlement of debts through compromise agreements or court decisions that exculpate the borrower from liability.
